nary_nodes.label: Ebola treatments trial begins
evidence: A trial of potential treatments for the species of virus behind the current deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has begun
The first patient has been enrolled in DR Congo

nary_nodes.label: Ebola cases and deaths confirmed
evidence: More than 1,400 cases and 438 deaths have been confirmed in the country, according to the WHO.

nary_nodes.label: No approved vaccines or treatments
evidence: There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo virus species of the disease, which is highly infectious.

nary_nodes.label: People recovering from disease
evidence: Even without approved therapeutics, people are recovering from this disease, but of course, we could save many more lives with safe and effective therapeutics in our toolkit.

nary_nodes.label: Trial launch significant step forward
evidence: the launch "represents a significant step forward, offering renewed hope to patients, their families, and affected communities".

nary_nodes.label: Ebola outbreak began
evidence: The current outbreak of Ebola in DR Congo began in May

nary_nodes.label: Public health emergency declared
evidence: The situation has been declared a public health emergency by the WHO

nary_nodes.label: Ebola case statistics as of July 1
evidence: there have been 1,460 confirmed cases in DR Congo, with 150 suspected cases and 452 deaths, as of 1July. According to the WHO, 213 people have recovered.

nary_nodes.label: Ebola cases in Uganda and France
evidence: There have also been 20 confirmed cases in Uganda, leading to two deaths, and one confirmed case in France, as of 1 July.

nary_nodes.label: Outbreak restricted to three provinces
evidence: Congolese health authorities have said the outbreak is currently restricted to three eastern provinces - South Kivu, North Kivu and Ituri.

nary_nodes.label: Pregnant woman tested positive for Ebola
evidence: the body of a pregnant woman tested positive for Ebola in the neighbouring Tshopo province. The woman reportedly died in Ituri, before her body was transported by motorbike to Tshopo's main city, Kisangani

nary_nodes.label: Individual fled isolation and tested positive
evidence: an individual suspected of having Ebola reportedly fled from an isolation unit in Ituri and later tested positive in the nearby Haut-Uele province.

nary_nodes.label: Contact-tracing efforts launched
evidence: Authorities are said to have launched contact-tracing efforts across Tshopo and Haut-Uele.

nary_nodes.label: Public gatherings banned
evidence: public gatherings were banned in both these provinces, along with neighbouring Bas-Uele and the capital, Kinshsasa, in order to prevent the spread of Ebola.

nary_nodes.label: Improved Ebola diagnosis
evidence: DR Congo's health ministry said it has improved diagnosis across the affected region. Previously, four laboratories were testing for Ebola, but that number has now increased to 10 .

nary_nodes.label: Outbreak potential to be largest ever
evidence: the current outbreak has the potential to be one of the largest ever, because it was spreading for weeks before it was confirmed to be Ebola.

nary_nodes.label: Conflict making outbreak difficult to tackle
evidence: International organisations also warn that conflict in eastern DR Congo is making it more difficult to tackle the outbreak.
